kana: もうしわけありません
use: A serious apology at work or to customers, for a mistake or an inconvenience.

example.romaji: Hontou ni moushiwake arimasen. Sugu ni naoshimasu.
example.ja: 本当に申し訳ありません。すぐに直します。
example.english: I'm truly sorry. I'll fix it right away.

notes: Stronger than sumimasen; the right level for your own work mistakes.

kana: もうしわけございません
use: Staff to customers, and in official apologies and announcements.

example.ja: お待たせして、申し訳ございません。
example.english: We're very sorry to keep you waiting.

notes: You'll hear it far more than you say it; moushiwake arimasen is enough for you.

src: お忙しいところすみません
ja: お忙しいところすみません
kana: おいそがしいところすみません
english: sorry to bother you when you're busy
use: Opens a request or question to a coworker, a clerk or a teacher.

example.romaji: Oisogashii tokoro sumimasen, chotto ii desu ka?
example.ja: お忙しいところすみません、ちょっといいですか？
example.english: Sorry to bother you, do you have a moment?

notes: A set opener; say it even if they don't look busy.

src: ご迷惑をおかけしました
ja: ご迷惑をおかけしました
kana: ごめいわくをおかけしました
english: sorry for the trouble I caused
use: Apology to coworkers or neighbours after you caused them trouble: a sick day, a mistake, noise.

example.romaji: Kinou wa yasunde shimatte, gomeiwaku o okake shimashita.
example.ja: 昨日は休んでしまって、ご迷惑をおかけしました。
example.english: Sorry for the trouble my day off caused yesterday.

notes: Meiwaku is trouble or nuisance. Casual: meiwaku kakete gomen.

use: Said when you need to look something up or ask someone before answering; staff say it a lot.

example.ja: すみません、ちょっと確認しますね。

notes: Casual: chotto mite miru. Staff often say kakunin itashimasu.

use: A polite yes to an instruction or request at work or from a customer.

example.romaji: Shouchi shimashita. Ashita made ni okurimasu.
example.ja: 承知しました。明日までに送ります。
example.english: Understood. I'll send it by tomorrow.

notes: Wakarimashita is fine with coworkers; kashikomarimashita is the shop-staff version.

use: Humble version of onegai shimasu for requests at work, on the phone and from staff.

example.romaji: Kochira no shorui, yoroshiku onegai itashimasu.
example.ja: こちらの書類、よろしくお願いいたします。
example.english: Please take care of these documents.

notes: Onegai shimasu is enough in daily life.

english: I'll think it over; we'll consider it
use: A business reply to a proposal or sales pitch; often a soft no.

example.romaji: Sou desu ne, chotto kentou shimasu.
example.ja: そうですね、ちょっと検討します。
example.english: Hmm, let me think it over.

notes: Don't read it as a yes; a real yes sounds like zehi or onegai shimasu.

use: Staff and business people use it for thanks or before asking a favour; you'll mostly hear it.

example.romaji: Osoreirimasu ga, onamae o ukagatte mo yoroshii desu ka?
example.ja: 恐れ入りますが、お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか？
example.english: Excuse me, may I ask your name?

notes: Osoreirimasu ga at the start works like a very polite sumimasen ga.

use: Quick apology from men to friends or juniors; also a gruff thanks.

example.ja: すまん、遅れた。電車が止まってた。
example.english: Sorry I'm late. The train had stopped.

notes: Never to a superior. Sumanai is an older, stiffer version.

use: Plain-form apology, often from men or older people to friends, family or juniors.

example.romaji: Isogashii no ni, moushiwake nai na.
example.ja: 忙しいのに、申し訳ないな。
example.english: Sorry to put you out when you're busy.

examplePolite.ja: お忙しいのに、申し訳ありません。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry to trouble you when you're busy.

notes: Also 'I feel bad': kare ni moushiwake nai (I feel bad toward him).

use: Pleading with someone close after hurting them, or a playful 'go easy on me'.

example.ja: 本当にごめん。お願い、許して。
example.english: I'm really sorry. Please forgive me.

examplePolite.romaji: Hontou ni sumimasen deshita. Douka yurushite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 本当にすみませんでした。どうか許してください。
examplePolite.english: I'm truly sorry. Please forgive me.

notes: Heavy for everyday slips, where gomen is enough.

english: I'm well, thank you; thanks to you
use: Polite answer when asked how you or your family are, or when congratulated.

example.romaji: Okagesama de, kodomo mo genki desu.
example.ja: おかげさまで、子供も元気です。
example.english: We're well, thank you. The kids are fine too.

notes: Thanks for general goodwill, not for something they actually did.

english: I've still got a long way to go
use: Modest reply to praise, especially of your Japanese; start with iie.

example.romaji: Iie, nihongo wa mada mada desu.
example.ja: いいえ、日本語はまだまだです。
example.english: Oh no, my Japanese has a long way to go.

use: Says something is far from done or good enough, about yourself or as a put-down to others.

example.romaji: Shiai ni katta kedo, mada mada da na.
example.ja: 試合に勝ったけど、まだまだだな。
example.english: We won the match, but we've still got a long way to go.

examplePolite.romaji: Shiai ni wa kachimashita ga, mada mada desu.
examplePolite.ja: 試合には勝ちましたが、まだまだです。
examplePolite.english: We won the match, but we've still got a long way to go.

notes: Also 'still lots more': mada mada aru (there's plenty left).

use: Humble way to talk about your own help, usually in oyaku ni tatete ureshii (glad I could help).

example.romaji: Oyaku ni tatete yokatta. Mata itsu demo itte ne.
example.ja: お役に立ててよかった。またいつでも言ってね。
example.english: Glad I could help. Ask me anytime.

examplePolite.romaji: Oyaku ni tatete ureshii desu. Mata itsu demo douzo.
examplePolite.ja: お役に立ててうれしいです。またいつでもどうぞ。
examplePolite.english: I'm glad I could help. Feel free to ask anytime.

notes: Plain yaku ni tatsu means 'be useful': kono apuri, yaku ni tatsu yo.
